$comment: Generated by scripts/gen-edge-cases.mjs from docs/spec/countersign-blueprint.md §12. `status`, `blockedReason` and `notes` are hand-maintained and preserved across regeneration. Test references are NOT stored here: scripts/ec-coverage.mjs scans the test tree for `EC-<GROUP>-<N>` markers and generates docs/EDGE_CASES.md from the result.

cases.scenario: Partial capture (one of two shipments)
cases.detection: Shipment covers a subset of lines
cases.handling: captureAuthorization with an allocated amount, final_capture=false; the remainder stays authorized
cases.userFacing: Receipt: "Charged $60 for 1 of 2 items; $40 still held"
cases.notes: The largest-remainder split that makes two partial captures sum exactly to the authorization is done and property-tested (packages/core/test/core.test.ts). The orchestrator that issues the two captures is WP-11.

cases.scenario: Final partial capture leaves money uncaptured
cases.handling: Capture with final_capture=true; PayPal releases the rest [B12]; ledger RELEASEs the remainder

cases.scenario: Capture exceeds the authorized amount
cases.handling: Rejected locally (CS_VALIDATION) before calling PayPal; a higher amount needs a new mandate-checked attempt
cases.userFacing: Merchant: "Exceeds authorization. Create a supplementary charge (requires a new Gate check)"

cases.scenario: Capture PENDING (eCheck / review)
cases.handling: State PENDING; ship nothing until PAYMENT.CAPTURE.COMPLETED (or the reconciler)

cases.scenario: Capture DECLINED
cases.handling: Budget RELEASE; order PAYMENT_FAILED; notify the user; no automatic retry with another instrument (the mandate binds one instrument)
cases.userFacing: Buyer: "PayPal declined the payment. Nothing was charged. Update PayPal and retry"

cases.scenario: Partial refund
cases.handling: refundCapture({amount}), PayPal-Request-Id = cs:{cap}:ref:{refId}
cases.userFacing: Receipt shows refund lines and the net paid

cases.scenario: Multiple partial refunds summing above the capture
cases.handling: Rejected locally; PayPal would also reject
cases.notes: The SQL backstop exists (captures.refunded_minor <= amount_minor, packages/db/test/schema.test.ts). The local sum check and its CS_VALIDATION happen in the orchestrator, WP-11.

cases.scenario: Refund PENDING / FAILED
cases.handling: Retry once after 1 h with a new refund ID if FAILED (never reuse a failed refund's request ID with a different body); otherwise escalate to manual

cases.scenario: Refund requested after a dispute is open
cases.detection: An open dispute on the capture
cases.handling: Block direct refunds; route through accept-claim/make-offer so PayPal records the resolution in the case
cases.userFacing: Merchant: "Refund via the dispute so it closes the case"

cases.scenario: Refund of a multi-currency or rounding remainder
cases.handling: allocate() largest-remainder; the last refund takes the exact remainder

cases.scenario: Agent submits the same checkout twice (LLM retry)
cases.detection: Same l3_jti, or the same checkout_id+mandate_id
cases.handling: Unique l3_jti → second gets GATE_REPLAY; the same checkout with a new L3 returns the existing attempt/order if one is in flight
cases.userFacing: Agent told "already purchased: order ord_…"; no double charge
cases.notes: packages/db (WP-02). packages/db/src/schema.ts checkout_attempts UNIQUE (l3_jti) -> checkout_attempts_l3_jti_key and UNIQUE (idempotency_key); packages/db/src/repos/index.ts toRepoError maps 23505 on that constraint to GATE_REPLAY and on idempotency_key to CS_CONFLICT (AT-M2.4); packages/db/src/repos/attempts.ts findAttemptByL3Jti / findAttemptByCheckoutAndMandate; packages/db/test/schema.test.ts 'EC-IDEM-1: checkout_attempts has UNIQUE (l3_jti) and UNIQUE (idempotency_key)' plus 'AT-M2.4'. STILL OPEN: the live replay race needs a database and belongs to WP-10.

cases.scenario: Our server times out after PayPal created the order
cases.handling: Retry with the same PayPal-Request-Id [B14]; PayPal returns the earlier result
cases.notes: packages/paypal/src/client.ts retries a side-effecting call only with the same PayPal-Request-Id, so PayPal returns the earlier result rather than creating a second order. Tests: packages/paypal/test/client.retry.test.ts.

cases.scenario: Endpoint without idempotency support times out
cases.detection: Endpoint is in the non-idempotent list (IDEMPOTENCY.md)
cases.handling: Re-read state (GET order/capture) before deciding to retry
cases.notes: packages/paypal/src/client.ts has a per-endpoint policy: side-effecting endpoints are marked re-read-first, and an ambiguous failure re-reads state via GET before deciding to retry rather than blind-retrying. The full table is packages/paypal/IDEMPOTENCY.md, with unverified cells marked as such.

cases.scenario: Two worker instances process the same job
cases.detection: pg-boss singleton key + DB unique constraints
cases.handling: The second gets CS_CONFLICT and no-ops

cases.scenario: Human double-clicks "Refund"
cases.detection: Button disables on click + idempotency key from the form nonce
cases.handling: One refund

cases.scenario: Buyer genuinely wants two identical items on two occasions
cases.detection: Different L3 (new jti) and new checkout
cases.handling: Allowed if the budget permits; line_items quantity caps apply per checkout

cases.scenario: Webhook never arrives
cases.detection: Reconciler finds non-terminal objects whose PayPal state is newer
cases.handling: Upsert from GET; metric reconciler_fixes_total
cases.declaredTest: I: drop the event, run the reconciler

cases.scenario: Same event delivered several times (PayPal retries up to 25× over 3 days [V14])
cases.handling: ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING; return 200
cases.notes: The dedupe key exists as UNIQUE (paypal_event_id) (packages/db/test/schema.test.ts). The INSERT ... ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING ingest that relies on it is WP-12.

cases.scenario: Out-of-order (REFUNDED before COMPLETED; dispute UPDATED before CREATED)
cases.handling: Always re-fetch the resource; never downgrade the rank

cases.scenario: Forged webhook
cases.handling: 400, audit log, alert after 10/h
cases.notes: packages/paypal/src/client.ts verifyWebhookSignature calls POST /v1/notifications/verify-webhook-signature; an unverified event is refused before any processing. Tests: packages/paypal/test/client.disputes.test.ts.

cases.scenario: Our endpoint down for hours
cases.detection: PayPal retries; the reconciler covers it on recovery
cases.handling: Idempotent processing

cases.scenario: Webhook for an unknown resource (simulator, other app)
cases.handling: Store, mark ignored, no crash
cases.notes: A resource PayPal does not know about maps to PP_NOT_FOUND rather than throwing, so a simulator event or a foreign app’s webhook is recorded and ignored. Test: packages/paypal/test/client.disputes.test.ts ("404 -> PP_NOT_FOUND (EC-DSP-9 / EC-WH-6)").

cases.scenario: Verify-signature API itself down
cases.handling: Store the event unverified, don't act; retry verification with backoff; the reconciler still progresses state from GETs (safe because GETs are authenticated)

cases.scenario: Mandate expires between checkout creation and Gate
cases.handling: BLOCK VI_EXPIRED
cases.userFacing: Agent: "Your mandate expired at 11:59 PM IST. Ask the user to renew"
cases.notes: withinValidity with the library skew is done (packages/core/test/core.test.ts). Gate check 1, which is what actually refuses an expired mandate, is WP-10.

cases.scenario: Revoked after Gate ALLOW, before order create
cases.detection: The orchestrator re-reads mandate status in the same tx as order creation
cases.handling: Abort; RELEASE the reservation

cases.scenario: Revoked after authorization, before capture
cases.handling: voidAuthorization for each; RELEASE; the order is CANCELLED
cases.userFacing: Revoke modal: "This also cancels 1 pending order ($48.00)"

cases.scenario: Revoked after capture
cases.handling: The purchase stands (it was authorised when made); the user can request a refund via a merchant message
cases.userFacing: "This order was completed at 14:01 IST, before you revoked at 14:02. You can request a return"

cases.scenario: Expired before a split shipment's second capture
cases.handling: Captures against an existing authorization remain valid: the authorization was created under a valid mandate and the amount is already bounded. Documented rule. No new authorizations

cases.scenario: Vault token deleted at PayPal (user removed it in PayPal settings)
cases.detection: VAULT.PAYMENT-TOKEN.DELETED webhook, or a create-order error
cases.handling: Wallet → DELETED; all mandates → SUSPENDED; the Gate blocks
cases.userFacing: "Your PayPal connection was removed. Reconnect to continue"
cases.notes: A deleted vault token comes back PP_NOT_FOUND (packages/paypal/test/client.vault.test.ts). Marking the wallet DELETED and suspending its mandates, plus the VAULT.PAYMENT-TOKEN.DELETED subscription, is WP-12.

cases.scenario: User edits the intent after signing
cases.handling: Mandates are immutable; editing creates a new mandate and offers to revoke the old one

cases.scenario: Browser clock wrong by hours
cases.detection: n/a: iat/exp are set server-side in l2/prepare; the browser only signs bytes
cases.handling: Not affected
cases.notes: apps/vi sets iat/exp server-side in l2/prepare; the browser only signs bytes and never supplies a timestamp, so a wrong client clock cannot affect a mandate. Test: apps/vi/tests/test_verify.py.

cases.scenario: Server clocks drift between web and vi
cases.detection: /status compares Date headers; alert if > 5 s
cases.handling: Library skew of 300 s tolerates it [B2]; Render hosts are NTP-synced [U]
cases.notes: packages/core/src/clock.ts withinValidity applies VI_CLOCK_SKEW_SECONDS (default 300, the library default), and apps/vi threads clock_skew_seconds into verify_chain. Tests: packages/core/test/core.test.ts, apps/vi/tests/test_verify.py.

cases.scenario: Dispute arrives after the mandate expired
cases.handling: Defender verifies with at_time = capture time and now; the evidence states both
cases.userFacing: Packet: "Valid at time of purchase (14:01 IST, 5 Oct); expired 12 Oct as designed"
cases.notes: apps/vi/tests/test_verify.py::test_EC_TIME_3_at_time_is_flagged_as_not_honoured and ::test_EC_TIME_3_at_time_within_the_window_is_reported_as_such. PARTIAL: the pinned verify_chain (commit 356c296) reads time.time() internally and takes no clock override, so /v1/verify CANNOT produce a real as-of verdict. It returns the verification it did perform at now, plus at_time_not_honoured=true, the reason, and an advisory within_validity_at window check computed by vi-service. A real as-of verification needs a now parameter in the library (docs/HUMAN_TODO.md). Defender-side EC-TIME-3 (verify twice, at capture time and now, and state both in the packet) is WP-15.
cases.blockedReason: verify_chain at the pinned VI commit has no clock override (chain.py:166 hardcodes now = int(time.time())), so as-of-capture-time verification is impossible, not merely unimplemented. apps/vi returns the real verdict at now plus at_time_not_honoured:true. Upstream request raised as HUMAN_TODO H-08; see DECISIONS D-009.

cases.scenario: Price-lock boundary race (lock expires mid-Gate)
cases.detection: Gate check 6 uses one clock.nowSec() captured at Gate start
cases.handling: Deterministic

cases.scenario: Authorization expiry (29 days; honor period 3 days [V15])
cases.handling: Day 3: reauthorize if unshipped and within mandate validity; day 28: alert; on expiry: state AUTH_EXPIRED, RELEASE
cases.userFacing: Merchant countdown; buyer "Order cancelled: not shipped in time"
cases.notes: packages/paypal records that no PAYMENT.AUTHORIZATION.EXPIRED event exists, so expiry must be polled from expiration_time (docs/DECISIONS.md D-016). The honour-period cron and reauthorize logic are WP-11/WP-12.

cases.scenario: Dispute deadline in a different TZ
cases.handling: Stored UTC; displayed IST with label; the Bryntum timeline uses UTC internally
cases.notes: packages/core/src/clock.ts formatIst/formatIstHuman render IST explicitly with a fixed +05:30 offset (no tz database needed, and exact since 1945). Test: packages/core/test/core.test.ts.

cases.scenario: Mandate in INR, store in USD
cases.handling: BLOCK CS_CURRENCY_MISMATCH. We never convert inside the Gate: FX rates are not signed by the user
cases.userFacing: "Your limit is in ₹. This store charges in $. Create a $ mandate"
cases.notes: packages/compiler/src/compile.ts validates the compiled currency against the mandate's currency and never converts. A request naming two currencies raises a blocking ambiguity (src/ambiguity.ts::currencyAmbiguity) rather than picking one, because picking would be choosing a currency AND a number the user never wrote. Tests: packages/compiler/test/compile.test.ts, test/ambiguity.test.ts.

cases.scenario: Buyer's PayPal funds in another currency (PayPal converts)
cases.detection: Capture seller_receivable_breakdown has an exchange rate
cases.handling: Out of our control. The mandate binds the merchant charge currency and amount; the receipt notes that PayPal may convert
cases.userFacing: "Charged $48.00. PayPal may show this in ₹ at its rate"

cases.scenario: Zero-decimal currency (JPY)
cases.handling: toPayPalValue emits no decimals
cases.notes: Handled in packages/core (WP-01): MINOR_DIGITS drives toPayPalValue/formatMoney/ppAmountSchema

cases.scenario: Rounding in shipping/tax allocation across split captures
cases.handling: Largest-remainder; Σ captures == total exactly; property test
cases.notes: Handled in packages/core (WP-01): allocate() largest-remainder, property-tested to sum exactly

cases.scenario: Float creeping in from the LLM ("129.99")
cases.detection: zod refines integer minor units; the compiler converts strings via fromPayPalValue
cases.handling: Reject floats at boundaries
cases.notes: Every amount the compiler produces goes through fromPayPalValue, so a model emitting "129.995" is refused with CS_ROUNDING rather than rounded. packages/compiler/src/literal.ts and src/constraints.ts; test/literal.test.ts asserts the model-supplied string is parsed, never coerced.

cases.scenario: VI example helper uses float dollars
cases.handling: Our checkout JWT uses integer minor units (§8.3)
cases.notes: Compiled amounts are integer minor units end to end; the read-back renderer uses core.formatMoney, and the JPY (zero minor digit) case is pinned in a snapshot. Test: packages/compiler/test/readback.test.ts.

cases.scenario: Price rises between cart and Gate
cases.detection: Checkout JWT is locked; the merchant changes the catalog
cases.handling: The locked price holds until price_lock_exp; after that a new checkout is needed, the agent re-quotes, and the Gate re-checks the mandate
cases.userFacing: "Price changed from $120 to $128. Still within your $130 limit, so the agent continued" or "Now $135, above your limit. Blocked"

cases.scenario: Merchant tries to capture more than the checkout total
cases.handling: PayPal rejects; we reject first (EC-CAP-3)
cases.notes: vi refuses to sign an L3 whose amount is out of range (apps/vi/tests/test_l3.py). Rejecting a capture that exceeds the authorized amount locally is the orchestrator, WP-11.

cases.scenario: Price drops after purchase
cases.handling: No automatic action (out of scope); a merchant may refund the difference (partial refund)

cases.scenario: Out of stock after authorization
cases.handling: Partial capture of the available lines + void the remainder (final_capture=true on the last capture)
cases.userFacing: "1 item unavailable. You were charged only $60. $40 released"
cases.notes: products.stock has a CHECK constraint preventing a negative count (packages/db/test/schema.test.ts). Partial capture plus void of the remainder is WP-11.

cases.scenario: Out of stock with the CAPTURE intent (digital, or the C2 fallback)
cases.handling: Partial refund of the OOS lines

cases.scenario: Last-unit race between two agents
cases.detection: Row lock on products.stock at ORDER_CREATED
cases.handling: One wins; the other gets BLOCK GATE_OUT_OF_STOCK and the reservation is released
cases.notes: The CHECK prevents negative stock (packages/db/test/schema.test.ts). The SELECT ... FOR UPDATE decrement at ORDER_CREATED, and the 20-way race test, are WP-10/WP-11.

cases.scenario: Split shipment
cases.handling: One capture + one tracker per shipment; evidence lists both
cases.userFacing: Two tracking numbers on the receipt
cases.notes: The PayPal client supports one tracker per capture (packages/paypal/test/client.orders.test.ts). The per-shipment capture loop is WP-11.

cases.scenario: Split shipment under the CAPTURE intent
cases.handling: Track twice against the same capture; OOS → partial refund
cases.notes: Tracking twice against one capture is supported by the client (packages/paypal/test/client.orders.test.ts). The CAPTURE-intent fulfilment path is WP-11.

cases.scenario: Dispute on only one shipment's items
cases.handling: The router evaluates only the disputed capture/lines

cases.sectionTitle: Buyer remorse vs. true fraud vs. friendly fraud
cases.scenario: Buyer remorse: the purchase was in-mandate but the user changed their mind
cases.detection: The user uses "Report a problem" or files SNAD/OTHER; the chain is valid; the item matches
cases.handling: Router R-SNAD-OK → CONTEST. The UI suggests that the merchant offer a return (make-offer with REFUND_WITH_RETURN) instead of fighting, since that's cheaper than the $82 handling cost [V13]
cases.userFacing: Buyer: "This matched your signed limits. The merchant offers a return"
cases.notes: makeOffer with REFUND_WITH_RETURN is implemented and tested (packages/paypal/test/client.disputes.test.ts). The router decision that prefers an offer over contesting is WP-15a.

cases.sectionTitle: Buyer remorse vs. true fraud vs. friendly fraud
cases.scenario: True fraud: someone stole the PayPal account but has no device key
cases.detection: No mandate, so there is no Countersign order. A chargeback on a non-Countersign transaction → R-NOCHAIN-1
cases.handling: ACCEPT/manual. Countersign proves nothing it didn't sign
cases.userFacing: Merchant: "No mandate on this payment. Countersign can't help here"

cases.sectionTitle: Buyer remorse vs. true fraud vs. friendly fraud
cases.scenario: True fraud via a compromised device (malware drove the browser and signed a mandate)
cases.detection: UNAUTHORISED + valid chain; device was reported LOST after the mandate iat; webauthn present?
cases.handling: If webauthn UV was absent → R-UNAUTH weak → the router recommends ACCEPT above $50 (merchant setting). If UV was present → CONTEST, but notify the user to secure their device
cases.userFacing: Buyer: "This mandate was signed on 'Asha's laptop' with your passkey at 10:02 IST. If that wasn't you, report the device lost"

cases.sectionTitle: Buyer remorse vs. true fraud vs. friendly fraud
cases.scenario: Friendly fraud: the user claims "unauthorised" for a purchase they signed
cases.handling: R-UNAUTH-1 → CONTEST with the mandate packet + tracking + read-back text the user saw
cases.userFacing: The packet shows the signed read-back verbatim

cases.sectionTitle: Buyer remorse vs. true fraud vs. friendly fraud
cases.scenario: Agent-fault "fraud" claim: the user says "I never asked for this", but the agent bought within limits and against preferences
cases.detection: UNAUTHORISED/SNAD + valid chain + the preferences diff fails
cases.handling: R-SNAD-AGENT → honest refund. The user did authorise the limits, but the agent clearly missed the stated preference; fighting it would be bad faith
cases.userFacing: "Your agent bought size 9; you asked for 10. The merchant refunded you"

cases.sectionTitle: Buyer remorse vs. true fraud vs. friendly fraud
cases.scenario: Serial disputer (≥3 disputes in 90 days)
cases.handling: Flag on S-17; no automatic action (avoids unfair profiling); merchant decides

cases.scenario: Prompt injection in a product listing
cases.handling: Listings are wrapped as untrusted; the Gate blocks out-of-mandate L3s; velocity guard → SUSPEND after 3 consecutive BLOCKs
cases.userFacing: Chat: "🛡 Blocked: the cart was $999 but your limit is $130. A listing tried to instruct your agent"
cases.notes: The three injection payloads are seeded from one exported constant so the corpus and the seed cannot drift (packages/db/test/seed.test.ts). The agent-side defences and the Gate verdict are WP-13.

cases.scenario: Compromised agent (attacker controls the LLM loop or its server)
cases.detection: Many BLOCKs, unusual merchants, off-hours bursts
cases.handling: It can only sign L3s within L2 limits (the agent key is bound by the L2). Worst case = the full budget at allowed merchants. The user can revoke the agent (all of its mandates are suspended)
cases.userFacing: Push/email (stub) "Your agent was suspended after 3 blocked attempts"

cases.scenario: Agent private key leaked
cases.detection: Key used from an unexpected source, or a manual report
cases.handling: jwks_keys.status=COMPROMISED; all mandates bound to it → REVOKED; the Gate refuses its L3s; past L3s are flagged "signed before compromise at T" in evidence
cases.userFacing: "Agent key rotated; please re-approve mandates (1 tap each)"

cases.scenario: Agent key rotation (scheduled)
cases.handling: New key → user re-signs new L2s (the L2 binds the agent key); old mandates keep the old key until expiry
cases.userFacing: "Re-approve 2 mandates for the new agent key"

cases.scenario: User device key lost (browser data cleared, new laptop)
cases.handling: Device → LOST; enrol a new device (PayPal re-auth via a new setup token or a session check) → new L1; old mandates keep working until expiry (the agent key, not the device key, signs purchases) unless the user chooses "revoke all"
cases.userFacing: "This device is new. Reconnect PayPal to create a key. Your existing mandates still work; revoke them?"
cases.notes: Client half done: packages/vi-client maps a finalize failure to VI_SIGNATURE_MISMATCH rather than a generic error, which is the branch the re-enrolment UI hangs on (test/client.test.ts). The browser side — IndexedDB empty -> Device LOST -> new enrolment -> old mandates keep working until expiry — is WP-05.

cases.scenario: Issuer key rotation
cases.handling: New kid in JWKS; old kept as RETIRED (verify-only) until the retention end; on compromise: mark COMPROMISED, re-issue all L1s, mandates need re-signing
cases.notes: apps/vi/src/vi_service/keys.py: POST /v1/keys/rotate retires the current key and GET /v1/jwks returns retired public keys with a status field, so evidence signed by an old kid still verifies. Test: apps/vi/tests/test_keys.py (AT-M3.9).

cases.scenario: Merchant checkout key rotation
cases.handling: The Gate accepts checkout JWTs from ACTIVE or RETIRED (within not_after) kids
cases.notes: apps/vi/src/vi_service/verify.py accepts a checkout JWT from an ACTIVE or RETIRED-but-not-after merchant kid, per Gate check 5 in spec 8.10. Test: apps/vi/tests/test_checkout_jwt.py.

cases.scenario: KEK (VI_KEK) lost
cases.handling: Agent keys are re-created → users re-sign L2s. Issuer/merchant keys are re-created → JWKS keeps the public halves, so historical evidence stays verifiable. Doc: back the KEK up in Render env + 1Password
cases.notes: apps/vi/src/vi_service/keys.py derives agent keys from VI_KEK; with the KEK changed, agent keys are undecryptable and re-minting is the only path, while issuer/merchant public keys survive in JWKS so historical evidence still verifies. Test: apps/vi/tests/test_keys.py.

cases.scenario: Family member uses the agent chat on the user's logged-in laptop
cases.detection: Can't be distinguished by session alone
cases.handling: The agent can still only spend within existing mandates. New mandates need the device key plus a WebAuthn UV (passkey biometric/PIN; D4)
cases.userFacing: Signing prompts the passkey; the family member can't pass it

cases.scenario: Family member knows the device PIN and signs a mandate
cases.handling: Legally/operationally it's the account holder's authorisation. The evidence shows a UV-backed signature. The dispute is resolved as friendly fraud / household use
cases.userFacing: Settings tip: "Use a passkey only you can unlock"

cases.scenario: Household wallet with explicit sub-users (P2)
cases.handling: P2: per-member agents with lower caps under one wallet cap

cases.scenario: Multiple agents on one wallet spending concurrently
cases.detection: Two agents' attempts in the same window
cases.handling: Each mandate has its own budget; the wallet cap is serialised via FOR UPDATE on wallet_caps
cases.userFacing: Mandate cards show the per-agent spend; the wallet cap bar sits on the wallet page
cases.notes: packages/db (WP-02). packages/db/src/schema.ts wallet_caps (wallet_id PK, cap_minor, currency, period DAY|MONTH); packages/db/src/repos/budget.ts walletCapCheckIn/lockWalletCap (SELECT ... FROM wallet_caps WHERE wallet_id = $1 FOR UPDATE) and sumWalletSpend (SUM RESERVE - SUM RELEASE across every mandate on the wallet); packages/db/test/seed.test.ts 'EC-MA-1: multiple agents on one wallet' asserts the lock target is the wallet row and that spend is summed across two mandates. STILL OPEN: the 20-way concurrent race needs Postgres and belongs to WP-10 AT-M10.2.

cases.scenario: Agent A tries to use agent B's mandate
cases.detection: L3 signed by key A ≠ L2 cnf (key B)
cases.handling: verify_chain fails (L3 must be signed by the L2-bound key)
cases.userFacing: Gate log: "Agent key not bound to this mandate"

cases.scenario: One agent, many mandates (different merchants)
cases.handling: The agent picks the mandate per checkout; the Gate verifies the one presented

cases.scenario: Merchant fabricates a mandate for a customer
cases.detection: It can't produce an L2 signed by the user's device key (no private key)
cases.handling: Verification fails publicly

cases.scenario: Merchant reuses a valid L3 for a second charge
cases.detection: l3_jti unique; custom_id hash per attempt; the PayPal order invoice_id is unique
cases.handling: Gate replay block; for disputes, the router flags duplicate captures (R-AMT-2)

cases.scenario: Merchant ships something different from the signed checkout
cases.handling: R-SNAD-MERCH → REFUND. Our packet would *hurt* the merchant, so the Defender never files it as a contest

cases.scenario: Merchant fakes tracking
cases.handling: The packet labels tracking "merchant-asserted via PayPal /track" and makes no carrier-verification claim

cases.scenario: Merchant edits the LLM notes to add unsupported claims
cases.detection: The citation checker runs on the final text at file time
cases.handling: Uncited claims → filing blocked; the merchant can only file with checker-clean notes or template notes
cases.userFacing: "2 sentences lack a source. Fix or use the template"

cases.scenario: Merchant selectively omits the read-back or preferences that hurt them
cases.detection: The packet schema includes the read-back and preferences hash as required fields
cases.handling: The PDF renderer fails without them; the public verifier recomputes the L2 hash, so omissions are visible

cases.scenario: Merchant overrides an AGENT_FAULT recommendation and contests anyway
cases.handling: Allowed (it's their account) but the packet shows the router's result + rule ID; it can't be hidden
cases.userFacing: Merchant confirm dialog: "Router says agent fault. Contest anyway?"

cases.sectionTitle: Disputes: stages, deadlines, chargeback after refund
cases.scenario: Chargeback after refund (buyer refunded, then the bank charges back)
cases.detection: Dispute on a capture with refunded_minor ≥ amount, or PAYMENT.CAPTURE.REVERSED after REFUNDED
cases.handling: R-REF-1 → provide-evidence with PROOF_OF_REFUND [B16] + refund ID/date; budget ledger REVERSE entry for the audit
cases.userFacing: Merchant: "Already refunded on 7 Oct. Filed proof of refund"

cases.sectionTitle: Disputes: stages, deadlines, chargeback after refund
cases.scenario: Partial refund, then a dispute for the full amount
cases.handling: Evidence: proof of partial refund + contest the remainder per its own rule

cases.sectionTitle: Disputes: stages, deadlines, chargeback after refund
cases.scenario: Inquiry stage (INQUIRY)
cases.handling: Prefer send-message/make-offer; no filing needed unless status = WAITING_FOR_SELLER_RESPONSE

cases.sectionTitle: Disputes: stages, deadlines, chargeback after refund
cases.scenario: Escalated to claim/chargeback
cases.handling: Re-run the router; new packet version; deadline recalculated from the API

cases.sectionTitle: Disputes: stages, deadlines, chargeback after refund
cases.scenario: Pre-arbitration / arbitration
cases.handling: provide-supporting-info with the original packet + new facts; never re-file contradictory notes (packet versions are diffed)

cases.sectionTitle: Disputes: stages, deadlines, chargeback after refund
cases.scenario: Appeal after a loss
cases.handling: Strategist proposes an appeal only if new evidence exists (e.g. a late tracking update)

cases.sectionTitle: Disputes: stages, deadlines, chargeback after refund
cases.scenario: Deadline about to pass
cases.handling: Alert; at < 1 h auto-file is disabled (risk of a partial upload) and the merchant is told to file manually in the PayPal UI
cases.userFacing: Red banner with an IST countdown

cases.sectionTitle: Disputes: stages, deadlines, chargeback after refund
cases.scenario: Deadline missed
cases.handling: DEF_DEADLINE_PASSED; state → likely loss; post-mortem note

cases.sectionTitle: Disputes: stages, deadlines, chargeback after refund
cases.scenario: Dispute can't be mapped to an order (no custom_id, foreign transaction)
cases.handling: R-NOCHAIN-1
cases.notes: Client side is done: a dispute whose transaction PayPal does not know maps to PP_NOT_FOUND (packages/paypal/test/client.disputes.test.ts). The R-NOCHAIN-1 rule that turns that into "Not a Countersign order", and the custom_id join back to the order, are WP-15a and WP-11.

cases.sectionTitle: Disputes: stages, deadlines, chargeback after refund
cases.scenario: Two disputes on one capture (inquiry + chargeback)
cases.handling: Link both; one packet per dispute; consistent facts

cases.sectionTitle: Disputes: stages, deadlines, chargeback after refund
cases.scenario: Buyer cancels the dispute
cases.handling: Close CLOSED_WON (cancelled)

cases.sectionTitle: Disputes: stages, deadlines, chargeback after refund
cases.scenario: Evidence upload partially fails (file too big / type)
cases.handling: Validate locally first (jpg/png/gif/pdf, < 10 MB, ≤ 50 MB total [V8]); compress the PDF; retry
cases.notes: packages/paypal/src/multipart.ts rejects an unsupported MIME type or an oversize file locally with CS_VALIDATION, before any upload, using decimal byte limits (10_000_000 per file, 50_000_000 total). Tests: packages/paypal/test/client.multipart.test.ts.

cases.sectionTitle: PayPal outages, rate limits, sandbox vs. live
cases.scenario: PayPal API down (5xx / timeouts)
cases.handling: Fail fast; the Gate still runs; order creation is queued (pg-boss, retried with the same request ID) for up to 15 min while the reservation holds; after that, RELEASE and tell the agent
cases.userFacing: "PayPal is having trouble. We'll retry for 15 min; nothing is charged twice"
cases.notes: packages/paypal/src/circuit.ts opens a per-host circuit after 5 consecutive PP_UNAVAILABLE for 30 s and then fails fast with retryable:true; a 429 deliberately does not count as an outage because PayPal is up and merely throttling. Tests: packages/paypal/test/circuit.test.ts.

cases.sectionTitle: PayPal outages, rate limits, sandbox vs. live
cases.scenario: Rate limited (429 RATE_LIMIT_REACHED; the policy is unpublished [B15])
cases.handling: Backoff with jitter; honour Retry-After; the reconciler throttles itself to 2 rps; Judge Mode serialises runs
cases.notes: packages/paypal/src/backoff.ts backs off with full jitter and honours Retry-After; a 429 carrying Retry-After: 2 waits at least 2 s, verified with an injected clock and sleep. Tests: packages/paypal/test/backoff.test.ts.

cases.sectionTitle: PayPal outages, rate limits, sandbox vs. live
cases.scenario: OAuth token expired mid-flight
cases.handling: Refresh once (single-flight), then retry
cases.notes: packages/paypal/src/client.ts refreshes the OAuth token once on a 401 via a single-flight refresh, then reports PP_AUTH. Tests: packages/paypal/test/client.oauth.test.ts.

cases.sectionTitle: PayPal outages, rate limits, sandbox vs. live
cases.scenario: PayPal MCP server down
cases.handling: The Defender switches to direct REST for the same operations (getDispute, listDisputes); the agent tooling degrades gracefully

cases.sectionTitle: PayPal outages, rate limits, sandbox vs. live
cases.scenario: Webhook verify endpoint slow
cases.handling: Respond 200 after storing; verify async (EC-WH-7)

cases.sectionTitle: PayPal outages, rate limits, sandbox vs. live
cases.scenario: Accidental live credentials
cases.detection: PAYPAL_ENV≠sandbox or the API base isn't the sandbox host
cases.handling: Boot refuses
cases.notes: Handled in packages/core (WP-01): envSchema rejects PAYPAL_ENV=live; assertSandbox enforces it at call time

cases.sectionTitle: PayPal outages, rate limits, sandbox vs. live
cases.scenario: Sandbox vs. live differences
cases.detection: Documented in docs/SANDBOX-VS-LIVE.md:; (1) the dispute simulators, adjudicate and require-evidence are sandbox-only [S29];; (2) live merchant-initiated vault charges need PayPal approval/RDA [V9];; (3) live dispute deadlines and outcomes are decided by humans;; (4) negative testing is beta and sandbox-only [V12];; (5) the webhook simulator sends fake resource IDs [V14]
cases.handling: The code paths that call sandbox-only APIs live in paypal.sandbox.* and are compiled out when PAYPAL_ENV=live (not supported anyway)

cases.sectionTitle: PayPal outages, rate limits, sandbox vs. live
cases.scenario: Sandbox data reset or account changes during judging
cases.detection: Daily health job runs J1 at 06:00 IST
cases.handling: Alert Vedant; scripts/sandbox-bootstrap.ts recreates the personas

cases.scenario: Erasure request with an open dispute
cases.handling: PRIVACY_LEGAL_HOLD; scheduled for after resolution + window; the user is told the date
cases.userFacing: "We'll erase on 2 Jun 2027 because a dispute needs this record"
cases.notes: Unbuilt. WP-19 owns packages/privacy. The PRIVACY_LEGAL_HOLD code already exists in the registry (packages/core/src/errors.ts) and the schema has privacy_requests.legal_hold_reason (packages/db), but no behaviour and therefore no test yet.

cases.scenario: Export request
cases.handling: JSON zip of all rows + tokens + PDFs within 24 h (immediate in the demo)

cases.scenario: Public verifier leaks PII
cases.handling: Redaction: email masked (a*@…), no street address; raw-token download includes selectively disclosed fields only (SD-JWT)
cases.notes: Handled in packages/core (WP-01): three-filter logger redaction + redacted public verifier payload (S-18)

cases.scenario: LLM provider data
cases.handling: OpenAI API data-usage settings documented; no PII sent to the compiler beyond the intent text; product data only to the agent

cases.scenario: Pre-erasure notice
cases.handling: 48 h email (stub) before the retention purge, per DPDP Rule 8(2) good practice [B17]

cases.scenario: Cross-border transfer (India user, US hosting)
cases.handling: Disclosed in the notice; Render region chosen = Singapore [U: confirm Render region list in WP-00]

cases.scenario: OpenAI down / timeout
cases.handling: Compiler → manual constraint form; agent → "try later"; Defender → template notes (deterministic)
cases.notes: compile() maps a provider timeout or outage to LLM_UNAVAILABLE with retryable:true, and never returns a partially-filled CompiledMandate, which is what lets the UI fall back to the manual constraint form. Test: packages/compiler/test/compile.test.ts.

cases.scenario: Output fails the zod schema
cases.handling: One repair retry (repairToolCall / re-ask), then fallback
cases.notes: One repair retry with the schema issues listed, then a typed failure. A model answer that fails its zod schema never becomes a constraint. Test: packages/compiler/test/compile.test.ts.

cases.scenario: Hallucinated fact in the notes
cases.handling: Citation checker blocks it

cases.scenario: Cost runaway (agent loop)
cases.handling: isStepCount(12); per-user daily token budget; Judge Mode capped

cases.scenario: Model deprecation
cases.handling: LLM_MAIN_MODEL env; the eval suite runs on a model switch
